title: Workload census + annealing operator for safe batching parameter rollouts
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Goal: Build a production-safe component that (1) performs a lightweight workload census to summarize per-customer request distributions and (2) runs a continuous annealing operator that proposes and safely applies incremental batching/caching parameter changes with automatic rollback on safety signals. Scope: workload profiler, heuristics engine, simulation dry-run, canary rollout orchestration, safety gates (latency SLO, error rate, quality regressions), rollback/circuit-breaker, observability and runbook. Success criteria: 1) Recommend parameters that reduce per-token cost by >=8% on representative customers without increasing 95th percentile latency by >10% or error rate by >0.1%; 2) Fully automated canary apply + rollback path with observable audit trail and <10m mean time to revert on failed canary; 3) Clear dashboards for operators to inspect census buckets and applied parameter delta history. Approach: 1) Workload census: sample 72h sliding window, compute histograms for sequence length, tokens-per-request, arrival inter-arrival distribution (p90/p99 bursts), model family, streaming vs non-streaming, KV-cache hit estimate, prompt prefix reuse rate. Produce compact fingerprint (stable 5-field tuple) for clustering. 2) Heuristics and cost model: combine empirical per-token latency curves (from kernel profiler) with cost model (GPU occupancy, batching efficiency, KV cache hit benefit) to synthesize candidate parameter vectors (batch_size_cap, max_concat, batching_window_ms, prefetch_kv). 3) Simulation dry-run: replay sampled traces through a micro-simulator to estimate latency percentiles and cost changes; compute quality risk score by running the candidate parameter set against pre-defined eval prompt sets (subset per customer). 4) Annealing operator: propose incremental changes (no more than X% batch cap per apply), run staged canary (1% traffic -> 5% -> 25%), monitor safety signals, and either advance, hold, or rollback. 5) Safety gates: latency SLOs (p95/p99), application error rate, abnormal token generation deltas, eval quality delta threshold, and observability gaps (missing telemetry will halt rollout). 6) Auditing and traceability: every proposed change creates an immutable change record with pre/post simulation snapshots, canary windows, and link to PR/approval if a human override is required. Key trade-offs: - Aggressive batching gives cost wins but risks tail latency regressions for bursty arrivals; we limit per-apply step sizes and require simulation coverage. - KV cache interactions are non-linear; we conservatively bias heuristics to avoid cache-churn for customers with high prompt reuse. - Quality regressions are expensive; we tie quality checks to prompt-specific evals where available. Operational plan: - Phase 1 (profiling + heuristics): implement census + cost-model + offline simulator. - Phase 2 (operator + canary engine): build staged rollout, telemetry hooks, and rollback logic. - Phase 3 (automation): enable fully automated small-step annealing for low-risk customers; require PM/SE approval for high-risk customers. Deliverables: census service, heuristics library, simulator, operator workflows (API + console), runbook, dashboards. Risks and mitigations: - Insufficient telemetry: add graceful halt and require minimum sampling. - Simulator mismatch: conservative safety multipliers and initial small canary percentages. - Interactions with Dedicated capacity autoscaling: add explicit disable flags and dependency checks prior to applying changes.
comments: 2026-02-16: Kickoff sync with PM and Product Ops. Agreed profiling window = 72h and stable fingerprint tuple. Action: Aisha to prototype census extractor on customer-buckets; Diego to sketch simulator API.

2026-02-22: Prototyped census run against region-us-east-1 sample stream. Initial clusters show 3 dominant shapes (short-chat, mid-form, long-batch). Raw notebook: https://drive.google.com/example-census-notebook (internal).

2026-02-28: Design review with Runtime team. Feedback: expose preflight simulation to runtime scheduler so we can measure occupancy; keep per-apply delta <= 30% batch-cap and <= 20ms batching_window change. Recording: https://meet.redwood.com/rec/xyz

2026-03-03: Implemented micro-simulator and ran 10k trace replays. Findings: candidate batch increase to 48 reduced cost by 12% for short-chat cluster but increased p99 by 18ms under synthetic burst. Decided to cap step to 20% and require canary progression stop if p99 uplift > 8ms.
2026-03-05: PR opened for census service and simulator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2278. Added initial telemetry hooks to Datadog dashboard 'batching-census-v1'.
2026-03-08: PM review (Sofia Kemp): requested ability to opt customers into 'aggressive' tuning only after SE sign-off; added label 'requires-se-approval' for high-risk clusters.

2026-03-10: Load test on staging with canary orchestration running 1% -> 10% traffic steps. Canary failed on customer 'alpha-3' due to KV cache churn; operator automatically rolled back after 6m. Postmortem: need better cache-aware heuristics. Next: implement prompt-reuse estimator and conservative weighting.
Next steps: implement prompt-reuse estimator, add quality eval integration to simulator, harden rollback audit trail, and schedule ops-runbook walkthrough with SRE (target week 2026-W12).
